Spot premium quotations for imported cathode have remained at low levels over the past two weeks. The high stock levels in the country mean that the arbitrage window remains closed. However, the differential between SHFE and LME prices (including VAT) did narrow, to $193/t on average over the past two weeks from $373/t in the preceding two week period, as the LME price fell by more than the SHFE price. We have heard reports from market insiders that spot premium quotations for imported cathode were in a $30-70/t range, with most © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **May 2012** www.crugroup.com activity around $50-55/t, and spot SXEW quotations in a $25-60/t range. While the range remains low, it has widened in response to physical market becoming less oversupplied. This rebalancing of the market can be seen in the copper stocks in bonded warehouses, which are estimated at 600-630,000t in Shanghai and a further 40-50,000t in Nanhai. This represents a 35,000t decline compared to a fortnight ago. In part this was as result of reduced imports. In April Chinese refined imports amounted to only 272,903t, down from 345,667t in March and we believe May imports will also be down. Increased exports have also helped trim the bonded stock levels. Refined exports rose slightly to 27,420t in April, from 26,537t in March and were up massively from only 700t in February. Market insiders believe that exports in May will be up by a further 20,000t, as traders and smelters both increase exports for delivery to LME warehouses. The backwardation on the LME has prompted Chinese holders of cathode to lend it to the LME market to profit from both the SHFE/LME arbitrage but also the backwardation. Or, for those that are short on the LME to cover their positions. In response, LME Asian warehouse tonnages have almost doubled since their most recent low of 29,325t on 8th May, up by 26,675t to 56,000t on 23rd May, with most of the increase in South Korean warehouses. These opposite movements in Chinese import and export levels resulted in a 130,000t reduction in net imports in April compared to February. Scrap imports also fell, though less dramatically, to 370,919t gross weight in April from 430,076t in M

arch. # New subsidy schemes announced The Chinese central government realised that the economy is slowing down more rapidly than they thought after April economic data was released. Thereafter, on 19th May, Premier Wen Jiaobao said during his trip to Hubei that the government would make “ensuring growth” of greater importance. This means the government would modestly change monetary policy and support the economy. Generally, these policy changes will help demand recovery in end-uses in the rest of this year, although the lags in the changes translating into an impact on copper demand means the impact this year could be small. In the regular meeting of the State Council on 16th May, the government decided to subsidise energy efficient products to the tune of RMB36.3B. The details are: - RMB26.5B subsidy for the purchase of qualified energy efficient home appliances including airconditioners, flat panel TVs, refrigerators, washing machines and water heaters. The period for the policy to be in place is set at one year; - RMB2.2B subsidy for energy efficient lighting and LEDs; - RMB6.0B subsidy for cars with engine size below 1.6L; and - RMB1.6B subsidy for highly efficient motors. China provided several subsidy programmes that benefited copper consumption as part of the economic stimulus package following the 2008-09 financial crisis. These included a subsidy of RMB30B for energy efficient air-conditioners from 31st May 2009 to 31st May 2011. There was also the “White goods going to the country side” policy that expired of 1st December. China also introduced the scrappage scheme for home appliance from 1st June 2009 to 31st December 2011 that amounted to RMB30B and trigged RMB342B consumption from 2009 to 2011. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **May 2012** www.crugroup.com Thus, the new subsidy scheme for energy efficient products should be positive for the home appliance sector that is a major consumer of copper semi-fabricated products, as it has been suffering from the removal of the subsidy policy last year. Railway projects are struggling to be financed after the train crash tragedy that took place on 23rd July last year. The Ministry of Railways published measures on 16th May to attract private investment into the railway industry. The Ministry is itself raising RMB20B through issuance of a bond. It also has a RMB2 trillion credit line which it was granted by banks at the end of last year. Given these developments, the planned RMB400B investment programme in 2012 should have few problems in being achieved. This means that the construction of railway projects is likely to speed up, after the large fall in the second half of 2011. # Copper prices down on economic fears SHFE 3-month price SHFE inventory falling sharply

The official LME cash copper price fell below US$7,700/t to $7,631/t on 23rd May, its lowest level since 9th January. The average cash-to-3 month backwardation narrowed over the past two weeks to $50/t from just over $100/t as the squeeze of those short in the market continues to wind down. The price decline was due to the latest developments in Greece, where the likelihood of the country leaving the euro seems to risen by the day. The decline in cathode inventory in SHFE warehouses accelerated over the past two weeks, falling by 13,635t in the first week and a further 16,325t in the second week. This took stocks down to 157,489t and the almost 30,000t decline over the two weeks was the highest two week decline since May last year. As the price fell below RMB57,000/t on SHFE, mainly in response to the lower LME price but also to the weak domestic demand picture, the backwardation between the 3-month price and the cash-month price widened to average over RMB600/t over the past two weeks. This compares to an average differential of just under RMB100/t in the preceding period, as the increased exports to feed the LME squeeze saw increased demand for nearby metal in China. We expect that copper prices on SHFE will react to LME and macroeconomic developments and trade in a wider RMB53,000-58,000/t range over the last week of May and the first week of June. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **May 2012** www.crugroup.com ### **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Wan Ling (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2183 ling.wan@crugroup.com **Paul Settles (London):** +44 20 7903 2227 paul.settles@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 25th May 2012.
